9.01.t: 9.1 The Arthroscopy Set — Tell Them Apart
9.01.b:
MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "what is this telescope?"
- "A rigid rod-lens arthroscope, usually **4 mm** wide and **30°** angled, sitting in its sheath with light cable and camera (Campbell)."
- "Rotating a 30° scope scans about **three times** the field of a 0° scope; a **70°** scope sees around corners (Campbell)."

### Recognise it
- Angle of inclination = angle between scope axis and the lens face → **0–120°** (Campbell)
- **25° and 30°** scopes are used most; 70° and 90° look into the posterior compartments through the notch (Campbell)

### 30° vs 70° scope
| | 30° | 70° |
|---|---|---|
| Use | routine knee and shoulder | posterior knee compartments (Campbell) |
| Rotation | scanning effect | very large circle, central **blind area** ahead (Campbell) |
| Orientation | easy | difficult (Campbell) |

- Field of view → **1.9 mm = 65°** · **2.7 mm = 90°** · **4.0 mm = 115°** (Campbell)

- Rotating 30° and 70° scopes: field and blind area (Campbell)
- Small-joint set: 2.7 mm scope, shavers, burr, RF probe (paper)

### Sheath, trocar, cannula
- **Sheath** → carries the scope and the inflow; **6.0–6.2 mm** sheath gives adequate flow (Campbell)
- Capsule → No. 11 blade + **blunt trocar** (routine → fewer nerve injuries), or a sharp trocar passed carefully (Campbell)
- Lax capsule in instability → blunt trocar may fail → **sharp trocar** justified, but it can score the humeral head (Prof Amr Rashwan)

- Plastic cannulas with sealed ends → **less fluid extravasation** · flexible silicone cannulas with collars → stay in the portal, retract soft tissue (Campbell)
- Cannulas whenever sutures are shuttled → no tangling in deltoid or bursa (Campbell; Prof Amr Rashwan)
- **Switching stick** holds the portal while cannulas change; **Wissinger rod** makes an opposite portal inside-out (Campbell)

- Shoulder instrument set: probes, passers, graspers, cannulas (Campbell)

### Fluid — gravity vs pump
- **Lactated Ringer** → physiologic, better meniscal cell survival than saline (Campbell)
- Gravity → each foot of bag height = **22 mm Hg**; bag at 3 feet (≈1 m) ≈ **66 mm Hg** (Campbell)
- Pump → knee **40–60 mm Hg** · shoulder **40 mm Hg below systolic** · elbow and ankle 40–45 mm Hg gravity (Campbell)
- **Epinephrine 1 mg/L** in the irrigant → better view, tourniquet need ↓ **50%** (Campbell)

MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "what is this hooked rod?"
- "An arthroscopic **probe** — the extension of the arthroscopist's finger, the most used instrument after the scope (Campbell)."
- "Right-angled, tip **3–4 mm**, so it also measures lesions; I palpate with its elbow, not its tip (Campbell)."

### Tell them apart
| Instrument | Look for | Does |
|---|---|---|
| **Probe** | blunt right-angled hook, 3–4 mm | feels cartilage, meniscus, ACL tension; lifts the meniscus (Campbell) |
| **Basket punch** ("meniscal biter") | jaws with an **open floor** | bites tissue; pieces drop into the joint (Campbell) |
| **Grasper** | toothed jaws, **ratchet** on handle | retrieves loose bodies, holds flaps under tension (Campbell) |
| **Scissors** | 3–4 mm, straight or hooked jaws | cuts meniscal fragments; hooked pull tissue in (Campbell) |
| **Knife** | disposable blade, hooked, down-cutting or end-cutting | passed through a cannula; magnetic tip aids retrieval (Campbell) |

- Basket → **3–5 mm**, straight or curved shaft; angles **30, 45, 90°**, and 15° up- or down-biting (Campbell)
- Small bites → less force on the pins → fewer broken jaws (Campbell)
- **Double-action** grasper (both jaws open) → holds an osteochondral loose body that slips from single-action jaws (Campbell)

- Arthroscopic probe with rounded, blunt tip (Campbell)
- Basket punches, graspers and scissors (Campbell)

### Suture instruments
- **Suture passer** pierces tissue and carries a suture → Accu-Pass, Scorpion, Quattro (Prof Amr Rashwan)
- **Bird beak** → passes through labrum or cuff and retrieves the suture (Prof Amr Rashwan)
- **Lasso** → curved needle; monofilament **Prolene** fed through it shuttles FiberWire or Ethibond (Prof Maged Samy)

- **Knot pusher** → sliding knot (Duncan loop, fisherman's) first, then **3–4 half hitches** (Prof Maged Samy; Campbell)
- Sutures not sliding → no sliding knot; alternating half hitches only (Prof Maged Samy)
- Rule → **one** thread in the cannula while passing, **two** while tying → otherwise entanglement (Prof Maged Samy)

- Suture lasso and grasper pulling ACL stump sutures (Prof Amr Rashwan)
- Duncan loop sliding knot tied with a knot pusher (Campbell)

HIGH YIELD — Memory line
- **Probe feels · basket bites · grasper holds · lasso shuttles**

9.03.b:
MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "what is this hollow blade?"
- "A motorised **shaver**: outer hollow sheath, inner rotating cannula, matching windows; suction pulls tissue in and the blade cuts it (Campbell)."
- "Tips **3–5.5 mm**; burrs and abraders for bone — acromioplasty, notch, footprint (Campbell)."

### Shaver and burr
- Special blades → meniscus, synovium, cartilage; small joints → **2-mm** shaver and burr (Campbell)
- Foot pedal for speed and direction; intermittent reverse → less clogging (Campbell)
- Tip always **in view**, window located before the motor starts (Campbell)

- Blade opening pointed up or lateral → away from the PCL (posterior cruciate ligament) (Campbell)
- Acromioplasty → mark depth with the burr, ≈ **5–6 mm** = acromionizer diameter (Prof Amr Rashwan)
- Acromionizer on the cuff footprint → hole into cancellous bone → anchor **pulls out** (Prof Amr Rashwan)
- Footprint → shaver or rasp only, to a bleeding surface (Prof Amr Rashwan)

- Motorised shaver blades of different windows (Campbell)

### Radiofrequency (RF) wand
- **Monopolar** → grounding pad, current through the body · **bipolar** → current between electrodes at the tip (Campbell)
- Complications → cartilage damage, **osteonecrosis**, irrigant tissue damage (Campbell) · notch preparation → RF minimised for thermal cartilage injury; shaver first (Prof Maged Samy)
- Chondrolysis after shoulder arthroscopy → linked with RF, pain pumps, bioabsorbable anchors (Miller)

9.04.t: 9.4 ACL Drill Guides — The Over-the-Top Guide
9.04.b:
MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "this is used for over-the-top — what is it?"
- "The **femoral offset aimer**: its hooked tip sits over the back of the lateral femoral condyle — the **over-the-top** position (Campbell)."
- "The guide pin enters a fixed distance in front of the hook, so the tunnel keeps a **posterior wall** and never blows out (Campbell; Nagah)."
- "Offset = **2–3 mm + half the graft diameter** (Nagah)."

### Recognise it
- Cannulated shaft with a small hook or spike at the tip; offset in mm on the guide, e.g. **7 mm** (Campbell)
- Over-the-top = drop-off where a probe or angled curette **hooks** over the posterolateral femoral condyle; repeat to confirm (Campbell)
- Resident's ridge (lateral intercondylar ridge) mistaken for over-the-top → tunnel **too anterior** (Campbell; Prof Maged Samy)

- Tibial drill guide and femoral offset guide, 7 mm (Campbell)
- Over-the-top area, and graft stapled there in revision (paper)

### How it works
- Tunnel centre = offset in front of the back cortex → wall left = offset − half the reamer (Nagah)
- Example → 10 mm graft: 5 mm + 2 mm wall → **7 mm** offset (Nagah)
- Behind the wall → over-the-top, then the **popliteal fossa**; breach = **tunnel blowout** (Prof Maged Samy)

| Fixation | Minimum posterior wall |
|---|---|
| Suspensory | ≈ **1 mm** acceptable (Prof Maged Samy) |
| Interference screw | ≥ **2 mm**; screw compression breaks a thin wall (Prof Maged Samy) |

- Campbell → 2-mm posterior wall, ≈ 5 mm from the articular surface · Handbook → 2–3 mm wall
- Femoral tunnel height ≈ **40%** of the lateral notch; avoid the roof (Handbook)
- Clock face, right knee → **9–10 o'clock** (Prof Maged Samy) · 10:00–10:30 (Handbook)

- Femoral footprint: resident's and bifurcate ridges, arthroscopic views (Campbell; paper)
- Femoral tunnel: quadrant method on lateral X-ray, clock face (paper; Campbell)
- Tibial footprint behind anterior horn of lateral meniscus (Prof Maged Samy; Campbell)
- Tibial tunnel: percent of plateau width on CT, inclination on X-rays (paper)

### Femoral drilling routes
| Route | Guide | Tunnel | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Transtibial** | offset aimer through the tibial tunnel (Campbell) | vertical, **11–12 o'clock** | AP stable, rotationally unstable (Prof Maged Samy) |
| **Transportal (AM)** | offset aimer via accessory anteromedial portal | horizontal, **9–10 o'clock** (Prof Maged Samy) | knee flexed ≈ **120°** (Prof Maged Samy; Campbell) |
| **Outside-in** | rear-entry guide from the lateral thigh | exit **3–4 cm** above the lateral epicondyle | two incisions (Campbell) |
| **All-inside** | FlipCutter retro-drill (Campbell) | sockets, not full tunnels | adjustable loop → 9.6 (Prof Maged Samy) |

- Transportal → large drill bit, not only a wire, protects the **medial condyle** cartilage (Prof Maged Samy)
- FlipCutter → drilled into the joint, blade flipped, socket reamed **backwards** to depth (Campbell)
- Graft angle ≈ **90° to the PCL** at 90° flexion; no notch impingement in extension (Prof Maged Samy)

- Accessory medial portal for transportal femoral drilling (Prof Maged Samy)
- Flat-blade reamer making the femoral tunnel (Campbell)
- FlipCutter tibial socket with stepped drill sleeve (Campbell)

### Tibial guide
| Guide | Pin exit | Placement |
|---|---|---|
| **Elbow aimer** | anterior to the tip | slightly posterior to target (Prof Maged Samy) |
| **Tip aimer** | exactly at the tip | exactly at target (Prof Maged Samy) |

- Angle **55–60°** to the plateau → enough tunnel length (Campbell) · Handbook → ≈ 55° sagittal
- Exit → posterior edge of the anterior horn of the lateral meniscus, lateral border of the medial spine (Prof Maged Samy)
- Pin ≈ **7 mm anterior to the PCL**, 2–3 mm anterior to the medial spine peak (Campbell)
- Suspensory femur → **4 mm** drill through, length measured, reamer only **25–30 mm** (Prof Maged Samy)

### Insertion — transportal femoral tunnel
1) Clear the notch with the shaver to the true back wall; keep the tibial stump (Prof Maged Samy)
2) Probe the over-the-top drop-off; mark the point behind the ridge (Campbell; Prof Maged Samy)
3) Knee to ≈ 120°; offset aimer through the accessory medial portal, hook over the top (Prof Maged Samy)
4) Guide pin → drill → measure → ream to graft size; check the wall (Prof Maged Samy)

### "Over-the-top" — the other meanings
- Older BTB (bone–patellar tendon–bone) route → graft wrapped around the lateral condyle in a deep **trough** (Campbell)
- Physis-sparing child ACL → iliotibial band routed **over the top** behind the condyle (Handbook)
- Revision with a lost posterior wall → convert to **over-the-top** or suspensory fixation (Campbell)

PITFALL — "which instrument is used for over-the-top?"
- The probe or curette only finds the point; the guide that drills from it is the **offset aimer**
- Say → "**Femoral offset aimer: hook over the top, pin a few mm anterior, posterior wall saved.**"

HIGH YIELD — Memory line
- **Hook behind, pin in front, wall in between**

9.05.b:
MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "ACL interference screw and its types"
- "A headless cannulated screw driven **beside the graft** in the tunnel; it wedges the graft against the wall → **aperture** fixation (Campbell; Prof Maged Samy)."
- "Types: **metal**, **bioabsorbable** (polylactic acid), **PEEK** (polyetheretherketone), and biocomposite (Nagah; Prof Maged Samy; Campbell)."
- "Femoral screw = tunnel size; tibial screw **1–2 mm larger** (Prof Maged Samy)."

### Recognise it
- Headless, cannulated → passed over a guide wire parallel to the graft (Campbell)
- Bioabsorbable → **transparent** white, green or blue · PEEK → **off-white**, not transparent (Prof Maged Samy)
- Most popular fixation for **BTB** grafts; also soft-tissue grafts (Campbell)

- PEEK screws and screws in tunnels, X-rays (Prof Maged Samy)
- Titanium, bioabsorbable and HA-coated interference screws; metal-screw MRI artefact (papers)
- Metal femoral and tibial interference screws, lateral X-ray (Prof Maged Samy)

### Types — tell them apart
| | Metal | Bioabsorbable (PLA) | PEEK |
|---|---|---|---|
| Fate | permanent | persists ≥ **2 years**, fragments on removal (Campbell) | permanent; tell the patient (Prof Maged Samy) |
| Strength | reference | pull-out comparable to metal (Campbell) | — |
| Problem | softened head strips at removal (Campbell) | reaction, **tunnel widening** (Prof Maged Samy) · ream through it at revision (Campbell) | none special (Prof Maged Samy) |
| Today | — | rarely used | standard screw, has replaced both (Prof Maged Samy) |

- Bioabsorbable implants → osteolytic reactions; PEEK, biocomposite and metal less so (Campbell)
- Revision defects → stacked oversized absorbable or metal screws fill them (Campbell)
- Metal femoral screw → marked **MRI artefact** around the tunnel (Grassi 2016)

### Parts and sizes
- Femur **9 → 9** · tibia 9 → 10 or 11 = **1–2 mm larger** (Prof Maged Samy) · Campbell → tibia at least **1 mm** larger
- Fixation devices fail at **200–1600 N**; early weak link = fixation, not graft (Campbell)

### How it works
- Compression and friction at the tunnel mouth → **less graft motion**, less creep and widening (Handbook)
- Cons → screw breakage; strength and stiffness fall in the first 6 weeks (Handbook)

### Indications · contraindications
| Use it | Avoid it |
|---|---|
| BTB femoral and tibial plugs (Campbell) | posterior wall **< 2 mm** → suspensory (Prof Maged Samy) |
| Tibial soft-tissue fixation after cycling (Prof Maged Samy) | open physis → no screw across it (Prof Amr Rashwan; Handbook) |
| Femoral soft tissue, posterior wall intact (Prof Maged Samy) | soft bone → tunnel may "explode" (Campbell) |

### Insertion
1) Pass the **nitinol** wire before the graft; after it, graft fibres get trapped and cut (Prof Maged Samy)
2) Mark the graft at **25 mm** → depth in the tunnel known (Prof Maged Samy)
3) Screw through the accessory medial portal at the **drilling angle**; otherwise it twists against the back cortex (Prof Maged Samy)
4) Hold tension on the graft sutures; screw parallel to plug and wall (Campbell)
5) Tibia → cycle the knee, tension at **0–20°** flexion, pull hard, insert the screw (Prof Maged Samy)
6) Extra length → back-up **staple** or screw and washer (Prof Maged Samy)

- Graft tension → hamstrings fixed at 30° need **≈ 80 N** vs BTB **20 N** · tension falls up to **30%** unless cyclically preconditioned (Campbell)

- Screw over the nitinol wire, femoral tunnel (Prof Maged Samy)

### What goes wrong
- **Graft advancement** → tension lost unless the plug is held · **suture laceration** → put a suture opposite the screw-bone interface (Campbell)
- **Tendon laceration** → screw tip beyond the bone plug (Campbell)

- Screw breaks on insertion; posterior wall **blowout** → screw-only plan fails (Prof Amr Rashwan)
- Failure commoner at the **tibia** → screw must be larger there (Prof Maged Samy)

- Correct fixation versus graft pushed in by the screw (Campbell)
- Passing suture opposite the screw protects it (Campbell)
- Screw beyond the bone plug cuts the tendon (Campbell)
- Screw divergence, vertical tunnel and femoral blowout (Miller)

PITFALL — how much divergence is too much?
- Campbell → divergence > 15° → ultimate tensile load falls **50%**
- Miller → > **30°** femoral tunnels, > **15°** tibial tunnels
- Say → "**Keep the screw parallel; over 15° the hold falls by half.**"

### Tunnel widening
- Suspensory → **windshield-wiper** effect (Prof Maged Samy; Nagah) · interference → synovial fluid enters the tunnel; **polylactic acid** screws (Prof Maged Samy)
- High-speed reaming, fluid tracking → CT showed an **8 mm** tunnel become **14 mm** (Prof Amr Rashwan)
- Workup → CT of tunnels; correct and not widened → **one stage** (Handbook)

- Widened tunnels → **two stages**: bone graft first, ACL later (Handbook; Nagah) · posterior wall lost → 9.4

- Widened femoral and tibial tunnels on AP X-rays (paper)
- One-stage versus two-stage revision by tunnel status (Handbook)

PITFALL — two stages when the tunnel is wider than…?
- Nagah → **> 13 mm** · Handbook → **> 13–15 mm** · Campbell (Harner) → **> 15 mm**
- Campbell → one-stage and two-stage outcomes did not differ
- Say → "**Widened over 13–15 mm or malplaced and overlapping → graft now, reconstruct later.**"

### Metal vs biodegradable — the bank question
- Equal pull-out · PLA reacts, widens tunnels, fragments at removal · metal head strips · PEEK now standard → table above (Campbell; Prof Maged Samy)

HIGH YIELD — Memory line
- **Femur equal, tibia bigger, keep it parallel**

9.05.1.b:
- Headless, cannulated → passed over a guide wire parallel to the graft (Campbell)
- Bioabsorbable → **transparent** white, green or blue · PEEK → **off-white**, not transparent (Prof Maged Samy)
- Most popular fixation for **BTB** grafts; also soft-tissue grafts (Campbell)

- PEEK screws and screws in tunnels, X-rays (Prof Maged Samy)
- Titanium, bioabsorbable and HA-coated interference screws; metal-screw MRI artefact (papers)
- Metal femoral and tibial interference screws, lateral X-ray (Prof Maged Samy)

9.05.2.b:
| | Metal | Bioabsorbable (PLA) | PEEK |
|---|---|---|---|
| Fate | permanent | persists ≥ **2 years**, fragments on removal (Campbell) | permanent; tell the patient (Prof Maged Samy) |
| Strength | reference | pull-out comparable to metal (Campbell) | — |
| Problem | softened head strips at removal (Campbell) | reaction, **tunnel widening** (Prof Maged Samy) · ream through it at revision (Campbell) | none special (Prof Maged Samy) |
| Today | — | rarely used | standard screw, has replaced both (Prof Maged Samy) |

- Bioabsorbable implants → osteolytic reactions; PEEK, biocomposite and metal less so (Campbell)
- Revision defects → stacked oversized absorbable or metal screws fill them (Campbell)
- Metal femoral screw → marked **MRI artefact** around the tunnel (Grassi 2016)

9.05.3.b:
- Femur **9 → 9** · tibia 9 → 10 or 11 = **1–2 mm larger** (Prof Maged Samy) · Campbell → tibia at least **1 mm** larger
- Fixation devices fail at **200–1600 N**; early weak link = fixation, not graft (Campbell)

9.05.4.b:
- Compression and friction at the tunnel mouth → **less graft motion**, less creep and widening (Handbook)
- Cons → screw breakage; strength and stiffness fall in the first 6 weeks (Handbook)

9.05.5.b:
| Use it | Avoid it |
|---|---|
| BTB femoral and tibial plugs (Campbell) | posterior wall **< 2 mm** → suspensory (Prof Maged Samy) |
| Tibial soft-tissue fixation after cycling (Prof Maged Samy) | open physis → no screw across it (Prof Amr Rashwan; Handbook) |
| Femoral soft tissue, posterior wall intact (Prof Maged Samy) | soft bone → tunnel may "explode" (Campbell) |

9.05.6.b:
1) Pass the **nitinol** wire before the graft; after it, graft fibres get trapped and cut (Prof Maged Samy)
2) Mark the graft at **25 mm** → depth in the tunnel known (Prof Maged Samy)
3) Screw through the accessory medial portal at the **drilling angle**; otherwise it twists against the back cortex (Prof Maged Samy)
4) Hold tension on the graft sutures; screw parallel to plug and wall (Campbell)
5) Tibia → cycle the knee, tension at **0–20°** flexion, pull hard, insert the screw (Prof Maged Samy)
6) Extra length → back-up **staple** or screw and washer (Prof Maged Samy)

- Graft tension → hamstrings fixed at 30° need **≈ 80 N** vs BTB **20 N** · tension falls up to **30%** unless cyclically preconditioned (Campbell)

- Screw over the nitinol wire, femoral tunnel (Prof Maged Samy)

9.05.7.b:
- **Graft advancement** → tension lost unless the plug is held · **suture laceration** → put a suture opposite the screw-bone interface (Campbell)
- **Tendon laceration** → screw tip beyond the bone plug (Campbell)

- Screw breaks on insertion; posterior wall **blowout** → screw-only plan fails (Prof Amr Rashwan)
- Failure commoner at the **tibia** → screw must be larger there (Prof Maged Samy)

- Correct fixation versus graft pushed in by the screw (Campbell)
- Passing suture opposite the screw protects it (Campbell)
- Screw beyond the bone plug cuts the tendon (Campbell)
- Screw divergence, vertical tunnel and femoral blowout (Miller)

PITFALL — how much divergence is too much?
- Campbell → divergence > 15° → ultimate tensile load falls **50%**
- Miller → > **30°** femoral tunnels, > **15°** tibial tunnels
- Say → "**Keep the screw parallel; over 15° the hold falls by half.**"

9.05.8.b:
- Suspensory → **windshield-wiper** effect (Prof Maged Samy; Nagah) · interference → synovial fluid enters the tunnel; **polylactic acid** screws (Prof Maged Samy)
- High-speed reaming, fluid tracking → CT showed an **8 mm** tunnel become **14 mm** (Prof Amr Rashwan)
- Workup → CT of tunnels; correct and not widened → **one stage** (Handbook)

- Widened tunnels → **two stages**: bone graft first, ACL later (Handbook; Nagah) · posterior wall lost → 9.4

- Widened femoral and tibial tunnels on AP X-rays (paper)
- One-stage versus two-stage revision by tunnel status (Handbook)

PITFALL — two stages when the tunnel is wider than…?
- Nagah → **> 13 mm** · Handbook → **> 13–15 mm** · Campbell (Harner) → **> 15 mm**
- Campbell → one-stage and two-stage outcomes did not differ
- Say → "**Widened over 13–15 mm or malplaced and overlapping → graft now, reconstruct later.**"

9.05.9.t: Metal vs biodegradable — the bank question
9.05.9.b:
- Equal pull-out · PLA reacts, widens tunnels, fragments at removal · metal head strips · PEEK now standard → table above (Campbell; Prof Maged Samy)

HIGH YIELD — Memory line
- **Femur equal, tibia bigger, keep it parallel**

9.06.b:
MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "what is this small plate with a loop?"
- "An **Endobutton**: a titanium button flipped on the lateral femoral cortex; the graft hangs on its loop — **suspensory** fixation (Campbell; Prof Maged Samy)."
- "Loop **fixed** (15, 20, 25 mm) or **adjustable** (≈ 60 mm, shortened in place) (Prof Maged Samy)."

### Tell them apart
| Device | Look for | Holds |
|---|---|---|
| **Fixed-loop button** | oblong button, closed loop | loop slightly longer than needed → room to flip (Prof Maged Samy) |
| **Adjustable loop** | button with sliding shortening strands | tightened until graft depth is right (Prof Maged Samy) |
| **Cross-pin** | pin across the femoral socket through the graft | direct fixation (Campbell) |
| **Staple / spiked washer** | tines or spikes on the tibial cortex | soft tissue to bone; greatest holding power with plates (Campbell) |
| **Screw post** | screw with sutures tied round it | indirect fixation (Campbell) |

- Endobutton with fixed continuous loop (Prof Maged Samy)
- Adjustable-loop button (Prof Maged Samy)
- Button on the femoral cortex: drawing and X-rays (Prof Maged Samy; paper)
- Cross-pin fixation of the femoral graft (Campbell)

### Loop length — worked example
- Tunnel **45 mm**, graft **30 mm** inside → **15 mm** loop (Prof Maged Samy)
- Washer **3–4 mm** larger than the femoral hole if the hole exceeds the button (Campbell)
- Flip confirmed → pulling the graft does not bring it down; sutures run as expected (Prof Maged Samy)
- All-inside → sockets in femur and tibia → **adjustable loop** only (Prof Maged Samy)

### Aperture vs suspensory
| | Aperture (screw) | Suspensory (button) |
|---|---|---|
| Graft motion | low | **bungee** and **windshield wiper** higher (Handbook) |
| Pull-out | lower | higher (Prof Maged Samy) |
| Biology | — | better preserved (Handbook) |
| Widening | less | more (Handbook) |
| Revision | lower | higher → PITFALL below (Prof Maged Samy) |

- Campbell → studies conflict on revision; IKDC, Lysholm, Lachman and pivot-shift outcomes equal · hybrid → combines aperture and suspensory fixation (Handbook)
- Children → suspensory, hardware out of the physis (Prof Amr Rashwan; Handbook)
- Skeletally immature **MPFL** → no screw across the femoral physis; anchor in the patella, graft looped around **adductor magnus** (Prof Amr Rashwan)
- MPFL femoral point = **Schöttle's point** → line along the posterior femoral cortex, perpendiculars at the posterior condyle junction and the back of Blumensaat's line (Prof Amr Rashwan)

- Aperture (screws) versus suspensory (buttons) graft fixation (paper)

### Other devices
- Direct → interference screws, staples, washers, **cross-pins** · indirect → tape/titanium button, suture post (Campbell)
- Washer spikes spaced at the periphery → microcirculation to the graft (Campbell) · press-fit bone plug and anchors are also used (Nagah; Prof Amr Rashwan)
- **Internal brace** (thin FiberTape) → augments ACL repair until the graft matures (Prof Maged Samy)

- ACL avulsion: sutures through tibial tunnels tied over a **bone bridge**, or buttons (Prof Amr Rashwan)
- Blowout rescue → screw and washer from outside, or button on the lateral cortex (Prof Amr Rashwan)

- ACL repair with anchors, internal brace and buttons (Prof Amr Rashwan)

PITFALL — "the button failed — why?"
- Higher suspensory revision → likely a button **not properly flipped** (Prof Maged Samy)
- Endobutton can also break on tensioning (Prof Amr Rashwan)
- Say → "**Confirm the flip: pull the graft back and watch the sutures.**"

9.07.b:
MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "what is this anchor?"
- "A suture anchor carries sutures into bone through its **eyelet**, fixing tendon or labrum **without a bone tunnel** (Campbell)."
- "Metal, bioabsorbable, PEEK or **all-suture**; knotted or **knotless** (Campbell; Prof Maged Samy)."

### Parts
- Body (screw-in or tap-in) · eyelet · preloaded sutures · inserter with a **laser mark** (Prof Maged Samy; Campbell)
- Knotless lateral-row anchors carry a **shuttle loop** to load the sutures (Prof Maged Samy)
- Advantages → biocompatible, strong, easy, early rehabilitation; used most in the shoulder (Campbell)

- Anchor designs, and metal Bankart anchors on X-ray (papers)

### Types — tell them apart
| Anchor | Insert | Note |
|---|---|---|
| **Metal** (metal tip) | hammered or screwed (Prof Maged Samy) | protrudes → **anchor arthritis** (Prof Amr Rashwan) |
| **PEEK** only | **screwed**; hammering breaks it (Prof Maged Samy) | fails in cement at revision (Prof Amr Rashwan) |
| **Bioabsorbable** | — | osteolysis; linked with chondrolysis (Campbell; Miller) |
| **All-suture** | no rigid body | small diameter, less osteolysis (Campbell) |
| **Knotless** (PushLock, SwiveLock) | tapped to the laser mark | lateral row of a double row (Prof Maged Samy) |

### Insertion
1) Needle-localised **anchor portal** → 9.9 (Prof Maged Samy)
2) Anchor at ≈ **45°** to the bone — "**deadman's angle**" → resists pull-out (Prof Amr Rashwan)
3) Drive until the laser mark is fully under bone → no prominent anchor (Prof Maged Samy)
4) Tug the sutures → firm hold confirmed (Prof Amr Rashwan)

- Anterior anchor in external rotation, posterior in internal rotation (Prof Maged Samy)
- Lateral row → well down on the lateral cortex, hand raised → no tuberosity avulsion (Prof Maged Samy)
- Single-row anchors ≈ **5 mm** lateral to the articular surface (Handbook)
- Weak bone → anchors perpendicular, ≥ **6 mm** apart; old anchors were 2–3 mm apart (Prof Amr Rashwan)

- Medial-row anchor with sutures in the cuff footprint (Prof Maged Samy)

### Constructs
| Construct | Idea |
|---|---|
| **Single row** | one line of anchors; line contact (Prof Maged Samy) |
| **Double row** | medial row near cartilage + lateral row near the tuberosity → surface contact (Prof Amr Rashwan) |
| **Suture bridge** | medial sutures criss-crossed to knotless lateral anchors → cuff compressed (Prof Amr Rashwan) |
| **Mason-Allen** | rip-stop stitch → resists cut-through (Prof Amr Rashwan) |

- Small and medium tears → double row not routine · large tears → lateral row definitely advised (Prof Maged Samy)
- Single-row re-tear → bone–tendon junction · double-row re-tear → **musculotendinous junction** (Handbook)
- Bankart → anchors at 3, 4, 5 o'clock (right) or 7, 8, 9 o'clock (left) (Handbook)
- Campbell → at least **three anchors** below 3 o'clock · bony Bankart fragment **> 25%** → bone block, open Latarjet or cannulated screws, not anchors alone (Prof Amr Rashwan)

- Single-row versus double-row cuff repair (Prof Amr Rashwan)
- Suture-bridge double-row repair (Prof Amr Rashwan)
- Construct by tear shape and size (Prof Amr Rashwan)
- Arthroscopic Bankart repair with suture anchors (Campbell)

PITFALL — cement in an old anchor hole?
- Metal anchor in cement → may hold · PEEK in cement → does not (Prof Amr Rashwan)
- Bone too weak → transosseous suture with a giant needle, no anchor (Prof Amr Rashwan)
- Say → "**Weak bone: perpendicular anchors, 6 mm apart, metal if cemented.**"

9.08.b:
MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "how do you repair a meniscus?"
- "**Inside-out** → needles in cannulas from inside out through the skin; **outside-in** → needle from outside, Prolene shuttle (Prof Maged Samy)."
- "**All-inside** → a device fired inside the knee; one part anchors behind the capsule (Prof Maged Samy)."

### Which technique where
| Site | Inside-out | Outside-in | All-inside |
|---|---|---|---|
| Anterior horn | impossible | only option | impossible (Prof Maged Samy) |
| Body | ideal | yes (Prof Maged Samy) | — |
| Posterior horn, medial | very risky | possible with training | reserved for these (Prof Maged Samy) |
| Posterior horn, lateral | never | not safe, peroneal nerve | **classic indication** (Prof Maged Samy) |

- Peripheral tear **≤ 7 mm** with **< 3 mm** displacement → heals without sutures after rasping (Campbell)

- Three repair techniques with their devices (Prof Maged Samy)

### Inside-out
- Double- or single-lumen **zone-specific cannulas**; incision and retractor to catch the needles (Campbell)
- Cheap, reusable · pushes a bucket handle **reduced** (Prof Maged Samy)

- Inside-out sutures through cannulas, ipsilateral and contralateral portals (Campbell)

### Outside-in
- No special instruments → **green IV cannula** preferred to grey, less trauma (Prof Maged Samy)
- Prolene passed → retrieved via another portal → shuttles **FiberWire** or Ethibond (Prof Maged Samy)
- Lateral meniscus → mark the **posterior border of the fibula**; never enter behind it (Prof Maged Samy)

- Outside-in needle passing a suture, model (Prof Maged Samy)
- Skin line at the fibula guards the peroneal nerve (Prof Maged Samy)

### All-inside
- Two parts → anchor behind the capsule + stitch or bar on the meniscus (Prof Maged Samy)
- Fourth generation → low profile, suture tension, much stronger hold · needle stop at **14 or 16 mm** → avoids overpenetration (Campbell)
- Cost ≈ **4,000–5,000 EGP** per stitch; 4–6 stitches usual (Prof Maged Samy)

- Disadvantages → meniscal damage on deployment, hard vertical repair, cost (Campbell) · no needle exits → no vessel or exit-needle risk (Prof Maged Samy)

- All-inside repair devices (Prof Maged Samy)
- All-inside repair completed, arthroscopic view (Campbell)

### Stitch and steps
| | Horizontal mattress | Vertical mattress |
|---|---|---|
| Pull-out | weaker | **stronger** (Prof Maged Samy) |
| Number | fewer | more (Prof Maged Samy) |
| Best for | central tears, anti-rip | peripheral tears (Prof Maged Samy) |

1) Freshen the tear and meniscocapsular junction with the shaver (Prof Maged Samy)
2) Reduce; stitches from above flip the meniscus → later stitches from **below** (Prof Maged Samy)
3) Pull-test; add a stitch where tissue lifts (Prof Maged Samy)
4) With ACL → tie after graft fixation (Prof Maged Samy)

### Root repair — transtibial pull-out
- Stitches through the root (lasso or plain needles) + tibial tunnel at the anatomic site (Prof Maged Samy)
- ACL tibial guide scrapes the condyle; **root guide** avoids it; **4.5 mm** drill (Prof Maged Samy)
- Stitches tied over the anterior **bone bridge** or a **washer** (Prof Maged Samy)
- Campbell → posterior roots (10–20%) transtibial + button · anterior roots (8%) all-suture anchors

- Meniscal root repair, arthroscopic views (Campbell)
- Root sutures tied over a washer with the ACL (Prof Maged Samy)

HIGH YIELD — Memory line
- **Front out-in · body in-out · back all-inside**

### Knee
| Portal | Where | For |
|---|---|---|
| **Anterolateral** | 1 cm above joint line, 1 cm lateral to patellar tendon | main viewing with 4-mm 30° scope (Campbell) |
| **Anteromedial** | 1 cm above joint line, 1 cm medial to tendon | probe, working (Campbell) |
| **Accessory medial** | just medial to the medial portal | femoral tunnel drilling (Prof Maged Samy) |
| **Posteromedial** | soft spot, 1 cm above joint line, 1 cm behind condyle | posterior horn, loose bodies, PCL (Campbell) |
| **Superolateral** | 2.5 cm above the patella, lateral to quadriceps | patellofemoral tracking (Campbell) |

- Too low → damages the anterior horn · too high → posterior horns unseen (Campbell)
- Hugging the patellar tendon → through the **fat pad** · infrapatellar branch of the saphenous nerve → the commonest cutaneous nerve injured (Campbell)

- Knee landmarks drawn before distension (Campbell)
- High versus low anterolateral portal (Campbell)

### Shoulder
| Portal | Where | For |
|---|---|---|
| **Posterior** | 2 cm inferior, 2 cm medial to posterolateral acromion | first, viewing (Prof Amr Rashwan) |
| **Anterior** | lateral to coracoid, upper border of subscapularis | working (Prof Amr Rashwan) |
| **Posterolateral (subacromial)** | ≈ 2 cm below lateral acromion, posterior | viewing in cuff repair (Prof Maged Samy) |
| **Anterolateral** | 2–2.5 cm below anterolateral acromion | working (Prof Maged Samy) |
| **Anchor portal** | just off lateral acromion, needle-localised | anchors, suture handling (Prof Maged Samy) |

- Posterior portal → soft spot between infraspinatus and teres minor (Prof Amr Rashwan)
- Never **medial to the coracoid** → vessels and brachial plexus (Prof Amr Rashwan)

9.10.b:
### General
- Complications **1–4.7%**; infection after knee arthroscopy **< 0.2%** · hemarthrosis → commonest postoperative complication (Campbell)
- Tourniquet **< 90 min** → no added morbidity · **> 90–120 min** → ischaemic muscle and nerve damage (Campbell)
- Fluid extravasation → compartment syndrome; gravity inflow, lower pressure, good outflow · popliteal vessels at risk in posterior meniscal repair; watch all-inside trajectory (Campbell)

- Partial meniscectomy → portal paraesthesia (saphenous branch), sinus, infection, early OA (Nagah) · synovial fistula → posteromedial portals; immobilise **7–10 days** (Campbell)
- Anchors, sutures, knots → chondral damage, synovitis, osteolysis, chondrolysis (Campbell)
- Bird beak too deep near the inferior glenohumeral ligament → **axillary nerve** palsy (Prof Amr Rashwan)

### Instrument breakage
1) Close the **outflow**, keep inflow → joint distended, less turbulence (Campbell)
2) Hold the joint still; keep the fragment **in view** (Campbell)
3) Search gutters, under the menisci, posterior compartment (Campbell)

### ACL implants and tunnels
- Commonest technical error → **tunnel malposition** · commonest complication → **arthrofibrosis** (Miller)
- Vertical tunnel → AP stable, rotationally unstable; anterior femoral tunnel → flexion loss (Miller)
- Graft **< 8 mm** in adults usually fails; aim 8–10 mm wide, 8–10 cm long · **≥ 8 cm** to be workable, 9 cm comfortable (Prof Maged Samy)

- Infection < 1%; washout with graft retention up to **85%** (Miller)
- Missed MCL, LCL, PLC or PCL injury → exclude before revision (Prof Maged Samy)
- Revision → CT tunnels, alignment, slope; osteolysis may force two stages (Miller)

- Considerations before revision ACL reconstruction (Miller)

### Shoulder implants
- Cuff re-tear → **musculotendinous junction** commonest site (Prof Amr Rashwan)
- Repair in abduction > **20–30°** → fails with the arm at the side (Prof Amr Rashwan)
- Over-tensioned Bankart → stiffness, arthrosis; missed bony Bankart → recurrence (Prof Amr Rashwan)
- Anchors placed too high on the tuberosity → fragment breaks (Prof Maged Samy)

PITFALL — "a screw broke in the joint — what now?"
- Do not chase it blindly; it drops into gutters or behind the menisci
- Say → "**Stop outflow, keep the limb still, keep it in view, retrieve it.**"

9.11.b:
| Question | Short answer |
|---|---|
| 30° vs 70° scope? | 30° scanning effect, field ×3; 70° around corners, central blind area |
| Field of a 4 mm scope? | 115° |
| Gravity pressure? | 22 mm Hg per foot; 3 feet ≈ 66 mm Hg |
| Basket vs grasper? | basket bites with open floor; grasper holds with ratchet |
| Over-the-top instrument? | femoral offset aimer: hook over the top, pin a few mm anterior |
| Posterior wall needed? | screw ≥2 mm; suspensory ≈1 mm |
| Transtibial vs transportal? | vertical 11–12 o'clock vs horizontal 9–10 o'clock |
| Interference screw types? | metal, bioabsorbable PLA, PEEK, biocomposite |
| Metal vs biodegradable? | equal pull-out; PLA reacts, widens tunnels; PEEK now standard |
| Screw divergence? | over 15° → ultimate tensile load falls 50% |
| Tunnel widening causes? | windshield wiper, synovial fluid, PLA screws, high-speed reaming |
| Revision with tunnel >13 mm? | two stages: bone graft first, ACL later |
| Types of ACL fixation? | press-fit, screw, suspensory button, cross-pin, staple, washer |
| Suspensory drawback? | bungee and windshield wiper; button not properly flipped |
| Avoid femoral blowout? | offset aimer, stay behind the ridge, 2 mm wall |
| Suture anchor parts? | body, eyelet, sutures, inserter with laser mark |
| Anchor angle? | deadman's 45° |
| Single vs double row? | line contact vs surface contact; suture bridge compresses |
| Posterior horn lateral meniscus? | all-inside |
| Root repair? | transtibial pull-out, tied over bone bridge or washer |
| Knee portals? | 1 cm above joint line, 1 cm beside the tendon |
| Shoulder posterior portal? | 2 cm inferior, 2 cm medial to posterolateral acromion |
| Instrument breaks? | close the outflow, keep inflow, fragment in view |
